questions.question: What is the central generalization requirement?
options: The model memorizes every training row
The model performs usefully on representative unseen examples
Training loss reaches exactly zero
The model uses more parameters than examples
questions.explanation: Generalization is useful behavior beyond the examples used to fit the model. Training performance alone cannot establish it.

questions.question: What is the central invariant for choosing between the two model families?
options: Choose the narrowest learning objective that can produce the required output under real constraints
Always use the model with the most parameters
Use a generative model whenever labels exist
Use a discriminative model whenever inputs are numeric
questions.explanation: The product output, available evidence, assumptions, latency, safety, and operational budget determine whether learning a richer distribution creates useful value.

questions.question: What should be named before choosing a model?
options: The product decision that consumes the prediction
The largest GPU available
A deep-learning architecture
A dashboard color
questions.explanation: The decision, user, and consequence define what prediction is useful.

questions.question: A churn score is consumed by a campaign that runs once each morning. Which serving pattern is the best starting point?
options: Request-time online inference for every page view
Scheduled batch scoring before the campaign runs
A stateful stream processor with second-level windows
Online learning after every customer event
questions.explanation: Batch scoring is simpler and efficient when predictions can be prepared within the product's freshness window.

questions.question: Why must time-series evaluation use forward-moving splits?
options: To balance every period to the same class ratio
To prevent future information from entering training
To remove seasonality from the observations
To increase the number of model parameters
questions.explanation: Each backtest must train only on information that would have existed before the evaluation period.
